description:
DECISION TICKET, reserved by the user ("User wants to DISCUSS the design before
implementation"). Nothing here is decidable by running anything.

## Now unblocked -- all three blockers are closed

fz-yj0, fz-usm.3 and fz-usm.4 are all CLOSED. The old blocked-by list should be
considered cleared.

## Premise verified at main 417c5b0b5

The GroundValue fold landed. `src/ground_value.rs:129`:

    pub enum MapKey { Atom(String), Int(i64) }

with the doc "This is the single canonical `{Atom, Int}` key shape:
`crate::types` re-exports it as `crate::types::MapKey` rather than defining its
own". So question (a) -- should map field keys be `GroundValue` rather than
atom/int-only? -- is still open and still meaningful: `MapKey` is the {Atom, Int}
projection, NOT the full GroundValue.

`MapSig` (src/compiler2/types/sigs.rs:110-112) is still exactly

    pub(crate) struct MapSig { pub fields: BTreeMap<MapKey, Ty> }

No `rest` axis. The doc at sigs.rs:103-105 still literally says "Keys are
concrete singleton values (atoms, ints, strs); arbitrary-keyed maps fall back to
`map_top`", so the lossy approximation is unchanged.

## Two questions to settle

(a) Should map field keys be `GroundValue` rather than the atom/int projection?
(b) Should `MapSig` gain a `rest` axis so a homogeneous `map(k, v)` is
    expressible, instead of falling back to `map_top`?

`@spec f(map(atom, integer))` currently errors
`expected 0 type argument(s), got 2 'map'`, which is the surface consequence.

## Drift and a small inconsistency to fold in

- The 2026-07-06 comment's "against HEAD 927c4b752" is stale; `MapKey` now lives
  in src/ground_value.rs, not src/types/map.rs as fz-yj0's body says.
- sigs.rs:103-105 claims keys may be "strs", but `MapKey` has only Atom and Int.
  That doc/code disagreement is worth fixing in whatever lands here.
title: Decide whether map field keys are GroundValue and whether MapSig gains a rest axis for homogeneous map(k,v)
